_comment: Model bank for scripts/gen_random_workload.py, keyed by the hardware
config's `profile.target`.  The generator draws networks from the platform
matching the chosen hardware, measures each against its profile CSVs, and
drops any it cannot resolve.
Per-model keys:
dispatch_deps_path -- repo-relative *_dispatch_graph.json; supplies the
dispatch ids and is copied into the workload.
profile_model      -- the <model> level of
gen/profile/<hw>/<target>/<model>/<basename>/...
profile_basename   -- the <basename> level; MUST equal the dispatch
path's parent directory name, because
profile_loader derives the basename from the path.
role               -- 'periodic' (runs at its own rate, see period_ms)
or 'sporadic' (laid into the gaps, no edges).
At least one usable periodic model is required.
period_ms          -- {min,max} for the model's PERIOD in ms: the rate
the task actually runs at, drawn once per
generation and then snapped to a multiple of the
fastest task's period.  It is DECLARED, not
derived from the network's runtime, because a
task's rate is a property of the loop it sits in
-- a 0.4 ms control MLP runs at 100+ Hz whatever
it costs, and sizing its period from its own
window is what produced a 283 ms control loop.
Copies of one model share its period and are
chained; models at different rates get no edges
between them, because an instance-i ->
instance-i edge only means anything at equal
rates.  Omitted, the period falls back to 2x-8x
the model's measured runtime.  Sporadic models
ignore it.
window_ms          -- optional {min,max} for the model's WINDOW in ms:
the deadline an instance has inside its period.
Drawn straight from this band, the same way the
period is, and NOT scaled by --min-scale /
--max-scale: a deadline is a property of the loop,
not a multiple of how fast the network happens to
run.  Scaling a 0.4 ms mlp_control gave it a 1 ms
window -- true to the measurement and useless as a
taskset, since nothing else can be scheduled
against a deadline that tight.  The draw is still
fitted to the period afterwards (see
fit_windows): a window never exceeds
period / --period-headroom and never drops below
the measured runtime.  Omitted, the window falls
back to measured runtime x U(--min-scale,
--max-scale).
count              -- {min,max} draws per generation; min 0 makes it
optional.  Multiple draws get _a/_b suffixes.
max_copies         -- optional ceiling on how many copies may be live
at once.  The count is drawn from `count` and
then clamped here, which is not the same as
narrowing `count`: clamping leaves the RNG
stream alone, so every other model in the
workload draws exactly what it drew before.
Copies of a model are concurrent by
construction -- shared period, chained
back-to-back inside the frame -- so this is how
a model that cannot run alongside itself says
so.  mlp_control caps at 1: two control MLPs a
frame is two loops flying one drone.
probability        -- optional chance in [0,1] that the model is drawn
at all; below it the count draw is skipped and
the model sits out this generation entirely.
Use it for a model that should show up now and
then rather than in most workloads -- `count.min:
0` only thins it to 1-in-(max+1).
variant_note       -- free text appended to the workload's _comment.

smolvlm_vision_v3.variant_note: 49 dispatches; profiled clean on CPU/DSP/HTA (no unsupported rows), HTA is the fastest whole-network backend.

smolvlm_vision_v3_bundles.variant_note: Alternative bundling of smolvlm_vision_v3 (97 dispatches). Every backend has unsupported dispatches, so no single backend runs it whole and its reference duration falls back to best-per-dispatch across CPU/DSP/HTA.

mlp_control.variant_note: Drone control policy, 7 dispatches, ~0.39 ms per instance on the scalar lane. fp32 only: this model has no int8 variant.

dronet.variant_note: Vision steering net, 24 dispatches, ~28.4 ms per instance on RVV and ~454 ms on scalar -- a 16x lane gap, which is what makes the periodic lane choice matter on this target.

yolov8_nano.variant_note: Detection load, 0-5 instances per generation: without gemmini it costs 629 ms serial on RVV (10.4 s on scalar) against dronet's 28 ms and mlp_control's 0.4 ms, so each instance stretches the sporadic span and the horizon with it. The count draw alone decides how loaded a workload is -- a sixth of seeds get none and stay a fast mlp+dronet control loop, the rest carry one to five detections. Five of them is ~1060 operations before a single periodic instance, so --max-ops will bind: the horizon shrinks toward one hyperperiod and the periodic tasks cover less of the sporadic span.

mlp_control.variant_note: fp32 build: the gemmini_q31 sweep profiles mlp_control.fp32, there is no int8 variant on disk.

dronet.variant_note: int8/gemmini build, matching the sweep_v8 profile data. The fp32 build at generic_riscv64/RVV/dronet.fp32 is the one the RVV-only FireSim configs use.

yolov8_nano.variant_note: Detection load, 0-5 instances per generation -- same count band as the spike platform's so the two RISC-V mixes stay comparable; gemmini brings its cost down but it is still the heaviest network here.
